description: The agent must: (1) Read guides/input-collection-guide.md Section 1 and initialize ~/.career-spotlight/ with analyses/, copies/, history/ subdirectories and a config.json. (2) Collect the three project sources, expanding the two directories into their constituent files, and use pandoc to convert lab_notebook.docx to text for the protein-folding project. (3) Assign 'highlight' priority to variant-calling and crispr projects, 'supporting' to protein-folding. (4) Detect that ~/.career-spotlight/analyses/variant-calling-pipeline.md is stale (mtime of source files is newer than analyzed_at in the front-matter) and mark it for re-analysis. (5) Run per-project analyses per project-analysis-guide.md, writing structured Markdown with YAML front-matter (project, slug, priority, analyzed_at, source_path, git_hash, mtime) and all 6 required sections to ~/.career-spotlight/analyses/. (6) Read domain-positioning-guide.md, generate a distinctiveness thesis, and confirm framing. (7) Archive the existing ~/.career-spotlight/report.md to ~/.career-spotlight/history/report-YYYY-MM-DDTHH-MM-SS.md with exact timestamp format before writing the new one. (8) Write new report.md using the aggregated-report.md template with all required sections including Meta-Themes, Top 3 Hidden Capabilities, Core Keywords, and Career Arc Narrative. (9) Archive all 4 existing files in copies/ to history/ with timestamp suffixes before writing new ones. (10) Write exactly 4 files to ~/.career-spotlight/copies/: resume-bullets.md, elevator-pitch.md, linkedin-summary.md, casual-intro.md — each with domain-specific content referencing the actual projects. The key proprietary traps are: the exact archive filename format (report-YYYY-MM-DDTHH-MM-SS.md), the 4 exact copy filenames, the YAML front-matter fields, the staleness detection logic, and the pandoc docx conversion requirement.
